question.problem:
Consider the function $y={x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}.$ Its derivative is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={x}^{5{x}^{2}-3}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y={x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =(5{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((5{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{2}-2)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(5{x}^{2}-2)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =10x\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+(5{x}^{2}-2)\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{5{x}^{2}-2}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\frac{5{x}^{2}-2}{x}+10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}(\frac{5{x}^{2}-2}{x}+10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{5{x}^{2}-2}(\frac{5{x}^{2}-2}{x}+\frac{10{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{5{x}^{2}-3}(5{x}^{2}+10{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=5{x}^{2}+10{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2.$
